title: Offshift oncall handover and follow-ups — Lena Park
content:
Shift: 23:30–07:30 (overnight) — notes for morning handoff.
Owner: Lena Park (eng-sre) — quick personal scratchpad, not official postmortem.

Quick TL;DR:
- Night had 2 pages. Both resolved to degraded queuing on region-eu-prod GPU pool (node eviction + slow fallback).
- Root cause still aliased to recent kubelet upgrade flag + GPU driver flakiness under pressure.
- Immediate mitigations used: routed heavy requests to eu-standby pool, increased eviction threshold, temporary scale-up (3 nodes).
- Follow-ups assigned below (runbook edits, monitoring alerts, blameless RCA next week).

Pages timeline (rough):
- 00:12 PD page: high p99 latency for /v1/generate on eu-prod (pager: latency-alerts).
  - Alert details: p99 > 1.4s for 5m.
  - First reaction: checked infra grafana (latency spike aligned with high GPU utilization).
  - Quick fix: activated route policy -> eu-standby (10:05 UTC).
  - Outcome: latency back to baseline in ~3m.
  - Note: my temporary route policy still active; must revert after canary validation (TODO below).

- 01:05 PD page: node eviction events (kubelet) > 2 nodes in eu-prod reported OOMKilled for nvidia-gpu-plugin (pager: infra-node-events).
  - Logs: dmesg shows GPU driver reset, kubelet eviction scanning started.
  - Action: forced cordon of 2 affected nodes, scaled up 3 replacement nodes from reserved pool, drained, and reprovisioned workloads.
  - Observed: one model server failed to rehydrate KV cache quickly (long cold start) causing brief tail latency. Mitigated by cold-cache warmup script (ran manually).

Notes/observations: 
- Pattern: driver resets -> kubelet eviction -> pod restarts -> burst of requests land on fewer pods -> p99 spikes.
- This aligns with recent kubelet v1.28.3 -> 1.28.6 rollout in eu-prod earlier tonight (PR infra: INF-2143).
- Happened during a regional batch of large seq requests (long-context LLM runs) — workload stress amplified driver bug.

Immediate TODOs (my priority list):
- [ ] Revert temporary routing change once morning canary verifies eu-standby stability (owner: me).
- [ ] Add temporary alert suppression rule for the specific p99 blip caused during node recovery so it doesn't page again while we're remediating (owner: Omar).
- [ ] Run synthetic E2E canary for long-context workloads across eu-prod -> eu-standby path (owner: Ruth).
- [ ] Document warmup script into the serving-runtime runbook and make it runnable as an automation (owner: me / infra-eng).
- [ ] Add a healthcheck to model server that verifies KV cache population within X seconds (proposal in INF-2143) (owner: product-serving).

Runbook gaps I noticed (actionable):
- Warmup steps for large-context models are ad-hoc; add explicit step-by-step with commands + required env vars.
- No explicit playbook for GPU driver reset during heavy batch workloads (we have node-restart but not driver-reset mitigation steps).
- Eviction thresholds for GPU nodes are conservative; consider raising thresholds or preemptive scale policy for scheduled high-seq batches.

Commands I ran (for context):
- kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted --namespace=redwood-serving | tail -n 30
- kubectl cordon gpu-node-12-eu-prod && kubectl drain gpu-node-12-eu-prod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group eu-gpu-pool --desired-capacity 5
- ./scripts/warmup_cache.sh --model redwood-xxl --instances 3 --timeout 300

Data I pulled (timestamps matched to pages):
- Grafana dashboard snapshot: latency_curve_eu_2026-03-16_00-10.png (uploaded to /tmp, will attach to postmortem).
- Node metrics: gpu-reset-count increased from 0->2 between 00:00–01:00 UTC.

Questions for oncoming shift / things to triage:
- Can we confirm if any other regions rolled kubelet upgrades at the same time? If yes, check for correlated events.
- Is the driver vendor rolling a patch for resets — any open ticket with them? (I flagged SOC, awaiting vendor reply).
- Are there any customer-facing SLA impacts logged (CS ticket open?) — link unknown, please search JIRA for INF-INC* or PD-4728.

Proposed medium term work (for backlog):
- Add a proactive autoscaler that watches model long-seq workload signals and pre-warms capacity.
- Improve model server startup to stream KV warming asynchronously to avoid blocking latency-critical requests.
- Add a post-deploy smoke test for infra kubelet+driver compatibility for each region before rollout.

Handoff checklist (for morning person):
- [ ] Validate eu-standby can handle routed traffic (run the synthetic long-seq canary).
- [ ] Confirm vendor SOC response re driver resets (if received, paste link).
- [ ] Sweep alerts: mark PD-4728 and INF-2143 watchers, add owners for follow-ups.
- [ ] Re-enable normal routing if canary stable for 15m.
- [ ] Create a short ticket that captures the warmup automation + runbook edits (put in INF backlog).

Misc quick notes / personal reminders: 
- Coffee. Bring decaf next night shift. 
- Check inbox for 'driver-rollback' thread from infra-team.

End-of-shift status:
- eu-prod normalized, temporary routing still active (controlled route: eu->eu-standby).
- 3 replacement nodes healthy, drained nodes reprovisioning.
- No open customer-availability incidents as of 07:10.

If anything wakes you, poke me in #oncall-lena (Slack) or call me — phone in 1Password.

— Lena

(Working notes; will convert to official incident RCA if we decide to escalate)
